title: In Joshua 10 How Can We Apply Joshuas Example Of Seeking Gods Help In Our Own Challenges
paragraphs: Joshua’s Example of Seeking God’s Help: Lessons from Joshua 10

The story found in Joshua 10 is a dramatic account of faith, prayer, and divine intervention. Joshua and the Israelites face a coalition of five Amorite kings who have joined forces to oppose them. Outnumbered and facing overwhelming odds, Joshua turns to the Lord for help. The result is one of the most miraculous victories in the Old Testament, including the famous moment when the sun stands still.
1. Recognizing the Need for God’s Help
When the Gibeonites, allies of Israel, cry out for help, Joshua does not hesitate to act on their behalf. Yet, before taking action, he seeks the Lord:
And Jehovah said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thy hands; there shall not a man of them stand before thee. - Joshua 10:8 ASV

Joshua’s first response to a challenge is to listen for God’s direction. This teaches us to prioritize prayer and dependence on God when we face difficulties, rather than relying solely on our own strategies or strength.
2. Bold Prayers Rooted in Faith
Perhaps the most remarkable moment in the chapter comes when Joshua prays for the sun to stand still:

Then spake Joshua to Jehovah in the day when Jehovah delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel; and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; And thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon. - Joshua 10:12 ASV
Joshua’s prayer is audacious, demonstrating confidence in God’s power and willingness to act on behalf of His people. The Lord answers his request:
And there was no day like that before it or after it, that Jehovah hearkened unto the voice of a man: for Jehovah fought for Israel. - Joshua 10:14 ASV
This challenges us to bring our deepest needs and boldest requests to God, trusting that He is able to do what is impossible for us (Ephesians 3:20 ASV).
3. Acting in Obedience and Courage
Joshua not only prays, but also acts. He leads his army on an all-night march to Gibeon and attacks the enemy. God’s answer to prayer comes as Joshua moves in obedience:

And Jehovah discomfited them before Israel, and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and smote them to Azekah, and unto Makkedah. - Joshua 10:10 ASV
This reminds us that seeking God’s help does not mean passivity. Instead, it means taking steps of faith, trusting God to work through our obedience.
4. Giving God the Glory
Throughout Joshua 10, it is clear that the victory belongs to the Lord:

And Jehovah cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died: there were more who died with the hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword. - Joshua 10:11 ASV
Joshua’s story teaches us to acknowledge God’s hand in our victories and to give Him glory for the outcomes, rather than taking credit ourselves (Psalm 115:1 ASV).
5. Application for Today
Seek God First: Bring every challenge to God in prayer before acting (Philippians 4:6 ASV).
Pray Boldly: Ask God for big things, believing in His power and goodness (Mark 11:24 ASV).
Obey Courageously: Step out in faith, trusting God to work as you follow His leading (James 2:17 ASV).
Give God the Glory: Celebrate God’s work in your life and testify to His faithfulness (Psalm 34:3 ASV).
Conclusion

Joshua’s example in Joshua 10 reminds us that God invites His people to seek Him in every situation. Through prayer, faith, obedience, and giving Him glory, we too can experience God’s help in our own battles.
